English: 1 Now those who are believers should live according to the example of Christ, who gave himself up for us, so that we might have eternal life with God. 2 Those who are not believers should not judge those who are. 3 For our lives are hidden with Christ in God. 4 Christ will reveal his glory in us, and we will share in his splendor. 5 Let us not be proud or arrogant, but humble ourselves before God. 6 Let us not seek our own interests, but the interests of others. 7 Let us not think highly of ourselves, but instead look to God for guidance. 8 Let us not compare ourselves to others, but focus on pleasing God. 9 Let us not be lazy or idle, but work hard to serve God. 10 Let us not be selfish or greedy, but generous and compassionate. 11 There is no difference between Jew and Gentile, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian and Scythian, slave and free—for Christ is all, and in all. 12 Therefore, as God’s chosen people, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. 13 Bear with each other and forgive one another, just as the Lord forgave you. English: After him, Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another portion. After him, Meshullam the son of Berechiah made repairs across from his room.
Kiswahili: Baada yake, Hanania mwana wa Shelemia, na Hanuni mwana wa sita wa Salafu walikarabati sehemu nyingine. Baada yao, Meshulamu mwana wa Berekia alikarabati sehemu iliyokuwa mkabala na nyumba zake za kuishi.
Ekegusii: Hanania, mosinto o Selemia, na Hanuni, omomura o gatano na rimo o Salafu, abwo bakaagacha ensemo ende. Oyobwatetie abwo, i’Mesulamu, mosinto o Berekia; ere akaagacha ensemo ende yarenge ang’e nakanyomba kaye.

English: When the holy city was inhabited with unbroken peace and the laws were kept very well because of the godliness of Onias the high priest and his hatred of wickedness,
Ekegusii: Ekero Onia arenge Omokuani omonene, omochie oria omochenu nigo orenge n’omorembe n’okwama okuya, n’amachiiko nigo arenge kobwatigwa buya mono, ekiagera Onia nigo amoirogete Nyasae na akanga ebibe.

English: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
Kiswahili: Wana wa Naftali ni: Yaseeli, Guni, Yeseri na Shilemu.
Ekegusii: Na abana abamura ba Nafutali nabwo aba: Yaseeli, na Guni, na Yaseri, na Silemu.

English: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Yahweh and for the service of the king.
Kiswahili: Kutoka kwa wana wa Hebroni: Hashabia na jamaa zake, watu 1,700 wenye uwezo, waliwajibika katika Israeli magharibi ya Yordani kwa ajili ya kazi zote za Bwana na utumishi wa mfalme.
Ekegusii: Korwa ase Abaheburoni, Hasabia na abanto b’eamate yaye, elifu eyemo na amagana atano na abere (1,700), abanto abamanyete buya gokora emeremo yabo, bakabeekwa ensemo ya bosongo ya Yorodani gotenenera Abaisraeli ase emeremo yonsi y’Omonene na ey’omorwoti.

English: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” so that they might accuse him.
Kiswahili: na huko alikuwepo mtu aliyepooza mkono. Wakitafuta sababu ya kumshtaki Yesu, wakamuuliza, “Je, ni halali kuponya siku ya Sabato?”
Ekegusii: Na rora, narengeo omonto, okoboko kwaye kwagataete. Bakaboria Yeso, “Inee! Mboronge kogwenia ase rituko ri’Esabato?” Nigo bamoboretie igo erio banyare komosoera.

English: But Yahweh says, “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the plunder retrieved from the fierce, for I will contend with him who contends with you and I will save your children.
Kiswahili: Lakini hili ndilo asemalo Bwana: “Naam, mateka watachukuliwa kutoka kwa mashujaa, na nyara zitapokonywa kutoka kwa watu wakali. Nitashindana na wale wanaoshindana nawe, nami nitawaokoa watoto wako.
Ekegusii: Ee, aya nar’Omonene agoteeba: “Nonya nabasibwa b’oyore ne chinguru mbarusigweo, na egiasakoretwe noyore omotindi ngetoorigwe, inche Omonene ning’amereranie noyio ogokoamereria, nintoorie abana bao.

English: “How long will you judge unjustly, and show partiality to the wicked?” Selah.
Kiswahili: “Hata lini utaendelea kuwatetea wasio haki na kuonyesha upendeleo kwa waovu?
Ekegusii: “Inee! Ngoika ririri moragenderere konacha ebiina bitari noboronge? Ngoika ririri moragenderere gwanchereria abanto ababe?

English: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
Kiswahili: Lolote mkono wako upatalo kufanya, fanya kwa nguvu zako zote, kwa kuwa huko kuzimu, unakokwenda, hakuna kufanya kazi wala mipango wala maarifa wala hekima.
Ekegusii: Gento kende gionsi okoboko kwao koranyare gokora, gekore ne chinguru chiao chionsi; ekiagera agwo aase abakuure ase oragende, meremo ende tekaiyo, gose okorengereria, gose chisemi, gose obong’aini.

English: Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. February 22, 2011.
Ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Monunguno O Barema (February) 22, 2011.

English: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.
Kiswahili: mwili wake ukiwa umenawiri, nayo mifupa yake ikiwa imejaa mafuta ndani yake.
Ekegusii: ebirandi biaye biichire namabeere, na amauga ’omobere oye aichire nemeseto.

English: The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Kiswahili: Wana wa Helemu ndugu yake walikuwa: Sofa, Imna, Sheleshi na Amali.
Ekegusii: Abana abamura ba Helemu, omomura omwabo, nabwo aba: Sofa, na Imuna, na Selesi, na Amali.

English: I have dug and drunk strange waters, and I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt with the sole of my feet.”
Kiswahili: Nimechimba visima katika nchi za kigeni na kunywa maji yake. Kwa nyayo za miguu yangu nimekausha vijito vyote vya Misri.”
Ekegusii: Ngakunya chinsoko naende nkanywa amaache ’abaanto b’echinse ching’ao, ngakamia chindooche chionsi chia Misiri ne ribarato ri’okogoro kwane.

English: For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land,” says Yahweh; “but, behold, I will deliver every one of the men into his neighbor’s hand and into the hand of his king. They will strike the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them.”
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa sitawahurumia tena watu wa nchi,” asema Bwana. “Nitawakabidhi kila mtu mkononi mwa jirani yake na mfalme wake. Wataitenda jeuri nchi, nami sitawaokoa kutoka mikononi mwao.”
Ekegusii: “Bono tinkogenderera kororera abanto b’ense eye amaabera. Naama! Nindue kera oyomo agwe ase okoboko kw’oyomwabo, na ase okoboko kw’omorwoti oye; abarwoti babo mbasarie ense, na inche tingotooria nonya nomonto oyomo korwa ase amaboko abo.” Nabo Omonene agoteeba.

English: Don’t give water an outlet, and don’t give a wicked woman freedom of speech.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana ogotanga ekerama kegotwa tikegoiterera amaache, boigo tobaisa komwanchera omokungu omobe gokwana buna ere anchete.

English: These are the families of Naphtali according to their families; and those who were counted of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.
Kiswahili: Hizi ndizo zilizokuwa koo za Naftali; wale waliohesabiwa walikuwa 45,400.
Ekegusii: Echi nachio chiamate chi’egesaku kia Nafutali. Abaabaretwe nigo barenge chilifu emerongo ene na isano, na amagana ane (45,400).

English: Ministry issues drought adaptation tips for sustainable water use.
Kiswahili: Wizara yatoa vidokezo vya kukabiliana na ukame kwa matumizi endelevu ya maji.
Ekegusii: Eminisituri nigo ekorwaogosemia igoro yogwekomereria ekero kieguragura na yogotumia amache buya.

English: “If thieves came to you, if robbers by night—oh, what disaster awaits you—wouldn’t they only steal until they had enough? If grape pickers came to you, wouldn’t they leave some gleaning grapes?
Kiswahili: “Ikiwa wevi wangekuja kwako, ikiwa wanyangʼanyi wangekujia usiku: Lo! Tazama ni maafa kiasi gani yangekuwa yanakungojea: je, si wangeiba tu kiasi ambacho wangehitaji? Kama wachuma zabibu wangekuja kwako, je, wasingebakiza zabibu chache?
Ekegusii: “Abaibi gose abasakori baise kogochera botuko, aye nosirigwe kegima. Ekeene, nigo baraibe binde bionsi baganetie. Inee! Abasangereria b’amasabibu baare kogochera, tibarenge kogotigera nonya naria agotigara? Korende asore aye ababisa bao bagosiririe kegima.

English: thirty bowls of gold, four hundred ten silver bowls of a second kind, and one thousand other vessels.
Kiswahili: mabakuli ya dhahabu yalikuwa 30 mabakuli ya fedha yanayofanana yalikuwa 410 vifaa vingine vilikuwa 1,000.
Ekegusii: chibakuri chinke chiroisirie korwa ase chitaabu, emerongo etato (30), na echiroisirie korwa ase chifeta, amagana ane, na ikomi (410), naende ebikorero binde, elifu eyemo (1,000).

English: Then one day, there was a great storm. A flash of lightning pierced right to the bottom of the pool. The waters parted for a moment. The snakes saw the earth above, full of colours and shapes and feathered creatures. When the waters closed again, the snakes could not forget the beauty they had seen.
Kiswahili: Basi siku moja pakatokea dhoruba kubwa. Radi ilipiga na kupenya hadi chini ya dimbwi. Maji yakagawika kwa muda mfupi, wale nyoka wakaweza kuona ardhi kule juu. Waliona vitu vya rangi nyingi na vyenye maumbo tofauti tofauti. Waliona viumbe wenye mbawa angani. Kila kitu walichoona ardhini kilivutia sana.
Ekegusii: Bono rituko erimo, embura enene egatwu. Enkoba akabara mbaka nse yengoro eria yarenge namache. Amache akabagana ase chingaki nke igo. Ching’iti chiria chikarora riroba igoro yabo ribwate chirangi ao ao amo nemenyama yende yabwate amarionya. Ekero amache aria airanete amo naende, ching’iti chiria tichichieti kweba obuya boria chiaroche igoro yabo.

English: They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, with unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
Kiswahili: Usiku huo huo watakula nyama iliyookwa kwenye moto, pamoja na mboga chungu za majani na mikate isiyotiwa chachu.
Ekegusii: Ase obotuko obwo barie chinyama chiria chisambire nomorero, amo nemegati etabekiri memera, ne chinyeni chindoro.

English: It is a holy portion of the land; it shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who come near to minister to Yahweh. It shall be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
Kiswahili: Itakuwa sehemu takatifu ya nchi kwa ajili ya makuhani, wale wanaohudumu ndani ya mahali patakatifu na ambao hukaribia ili kuhudumu mbele za Bwana. Patakuwa mahali pa nyumba zao pamoja na sehemu kwa ajili ya mahali patakatifu.
Ekegusii: Oboremo obwo mbobe ensemo enchenu y’ense eye, bobe obw’abakuani abwo bare abakoreri b’Aase Aachenu bagotenena ase obosio bw’Omonene. Nao baraagache chinyomba chiabo, naende nao arabe aase aachenu ase Hekalu eraagachwe.

English: (I have certainly not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
Kiswahili: lakini sikuruhusu kinywa changu kufanya dhambi kwa kuomba laana dhidi ya maisha yake;
Ekegusii: Yaya, tinatigete omonwa one okore ebibe ase okomoragereria na komoganeria amakweri.

English: “‘“How weak is your heart,” says the Lord Yahweh, “since you do all these things, the work of an impudent prostitute;
Kiswahili: “ ‘Tazama jinsi ulivyo na dhamiri dhaifu, asema Bwana Mwenyezi, unapofanya mambo haya yote, ukifanya kama kahaba asiyekuwa na aibu!
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo agoteeba iga: “Naki enkoro yao ere nokogania okonene kw’ogwanchwa, ekiagera gwakorire aya onsi, ayare buna ogokora kw’omokuungu omonyaka otari korora obosooku.

English: I looked, and behold, you had sinned against Yahweh your God. You had made yourselves a molded calf. You had quickly turned away from the way which Yahweh had commanded you.
Kiswahili: Nilipotazama, niliona kuwa mmefanya dhambi dhidi ya Bwana Mungu wenu; mmejifanyia sanamu ya kusubu katika umbo la ndama. Mmegeuka upesi kutoka njia ile Bwana aliyowaagiza.
Ekegusii: Erio ’nkarora ng’a mwakorire ebibe ase Omonene, Nyasae oino: konya mweroiseirie omogwekano bw’emori onyititoire na kobombwa, na mwaonchokire bwango, mwatigire enchera eri’Omonene abachiigete mobwatie.

English: Who has believed our message? To whom has Yahweh’s arm been revealed?
Kiswahili: Ni nani aliyeamini ujumbe wetu, na mkono wa Bwana umefunuliwa kwa nani?
Ekegusii: Ning’o bwegenire amang’ana aya twaraaretie? Ning’Omonene amaanoreire okoboko kwaye?

English: For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana hili ndilo asemalo Aliye juu, yeye aliyeinuliwa sana, yeye aishiye milele, ambaye jina lake ni Mtakatifu: “Ninaishi mimi mahali palipoinuka na patakatifu, lakini pia pamoja na yeye aliye na roho iliyotubu na mwenye roho ya unyenyekevu, ili kuzihuisha roho za wanyenyekevu na kuihuisha mioyo yao waliotubu.
Ekegusii: Aya naro Oyio ore Igoro Mono, Oyio oragaambe goika kare na kare, Oyio erieta riaye n’Omochenu, agoteeba: “Inche nigo imenyete Aase aachenu are igoro mono, boigo nigo imenyete amo noyio enkoro yaye yeitirie na gwekeyia, erinde ninkore omoika bw’oyore omoitongo obe omoyia, na koa obogima ase oyio enkoro yaye yeitirie.

English: He who didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?
Kiswahili: Ikiwa Mungu hakumhurumia Mwanawe, bali alimtoa kwa ajili yetu sote, atakosaje basi kutupatia vitu vyote kwa ukarimu pamoja naye?
Ekegusii: Ere otarorerete Omwana oye amaabera, korende akamorua ase engencho yaito intwe twensi, inaki aramoche gotoa ebinto bionsi amo nere?

English: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
Kiswahili: Kama mtu yeyote akikataa kusikia sheria, hata maombi yake ni chukizo.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoonchora ogoto kwaye taigwera amachiiko, nonya n’ogosaba kwaye nigo kore okogechia.

English: Behold, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people from a land that is very far off: “Isn’t Yahweh in Zion? Isn’t her King in her?” “Why have they provoked me to anger with their engraved images, and with foreign idols?”
Kiswahili: Sikia kilio cha watu wangu kutoka nchi ya mbali: “Je, Bwana hayuko Sayuni? Je, Mfalme wake hayuko tena huko?” “Kwa nini wamenikasirisha kwa vinyago vyao, kwa sanamu zao za kigeni zisizofaa?”
Ekegusii: Tegerera! Abanto baane nkorera bare korwa ase chinsemo chionsi chi’ense, bakoboria: “Inee! Omonene tari ase Sayoni? Omorwoti o Sayoni tari aroro?” Omonene nigo agoteeba; “Nase ki abanto bangechirie nabeire nendamwamu ase ogosasiima emegwekano yabo ebombire amo ne chinyasae chiabo chingeni?”

English: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
Kiswahili: Mungu akasikia kilio chao cha huzuni, akakumbuka Agano alilofanya na Abrahamu pamoja na Isaki na Yakobo.
Ekegusii: Nyasae akaigwa ekerero kiabo, na akainyora okobwatana kwaye kw’ogotianania, okwo akorete na Aburaamu, na Isaka, na Yakobo;

English: He called for a famine on the land. He destroyed the food supplies.
Kiswahili: Akaiita njaa juu ya nchi na kuharibu chakula chao chote,
Ekegusii: Ekero Omonene arentete enchara ase ense, na asiretie chindagera chiabo chionsi,

English: And these two lots came for an appointed season, and for a day of judgment, before God, and for all the nations.
Ekegusii: Nabwo nigo bare gokora emeremo ase chingaki nebiro abio Nyasae achorete ase chinse chionsi.

English: He who keeps the law multiplies offerings. He who heeds the commandments sacrifices a peace offering.
Ekegusii: Ere oria obwatete amachiiko orure okorua okonene.

English: He said to them, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Every man put his sword on his thigh, and go back and forth from gate to gate throughout the camp, and every man kill his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.’”
Kiswahili: Ndipo alipowaambia, “Hili ndilo Bwana, Mungu wa Israeli asemalo: ‘Kila mmoja wenu ajifunge upanga wake kiunoni aende huku na huko kambi yote mwisho hadi mwisho mwingine, kila mmoja amuue ndugu yake, na rafiki yake na jirani yake.’ ”
Ekegusii: Ere akabateebia, Omonene Nyasae, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, oteebire iga “Kera oyomo oino abogorie omoyio oye o birende, agende aaria na aaria ase egetwori korwa egeita ekemo goika ekende. Kera oyomo aite onde bwensi aranyore, nonya noyomwabo, gose omosani, gose omogisangio”.

English: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,
Kiswahili: “Mfalme Agripa, najiona kuwa na heri kusimama mbele yako leo ninapojitetea kuhusu mashtaka yote ya Wayahudi,
Ekegusii: “Omorwoti Agripa, nerorire omonyene ng’a ninde negesio, ekiagera ninyekengere ase obosio bwao reero, ase amang’ana aria onsi nasoerwa n’Abayahudi.

English: But when the judge was dead, they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their fathers in following other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They didn’t cease what they were doing, or give up their stubborn ways.
Kiswahili: Lakini kila mara mwamuzi alipofariki, watu walirudia katika hali mbaya ya uovu zaidi kuliko baba zao, wakiifuata miungu mingine kuitumikia na kuiabudu. Walikataa kuacha matendo yao maovu na njia zao za ukaidi.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero omogambi oria akuure, abanto baba bakoonchoka na gokora amabe kobua aye’chisokoro chiabo chiakorete. Naende baba bakobwatana n’echinyasae chinde ching’ao, ase ogochikorera na gochisasiima. Tibatigete ogokora kwabo okobe okwo banarete gokora n’oboenenu.

English: He took all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the two kidneys, and their fat; and Moses burned it on the altar.
Kiswahili: Pia Mose akachukua mafuta yote yanayozunguka sehemu za ndani, mafuta yanayofunika ini, figo zote mbili pamoja na mafuta yake, akayateketeza juu ya madhabahu.
Ekegusii: Akaimokia ebitinya bionsi biareenge ase chinyama chi’enda, n’ebitinya bie riini, ne chinyigo chionsi ibere amo nebitinya bichitubete, Erio Musa akabisaambera ase egesasiimero.

English: She hasn’t left her prostitution since leaving Egypt; for in her youth they lay with her. They caressed her youthful nipples and they poured out their prostitution on her.
Kiswahili: Hakuacha ukahaba wake aliouanza huko Misri, wakati ambapo tangu ujana wake wanaume walilala naye, wakikumbatia kifua cha ubikira wake na kumwaga tamaa zao juu yake.
Ekegusii: Ohola tatigete obonyaka bwaye, boria anarete gokora korwa ekero arenge Misiri, ekiagera ase oboiseke bwaye abasacha nigo barenge gokora obonyaka nere, bagasiria obwekungi bwaye, bakaumora okogania kwabo okobe igoro ase are.

English: You make us turn back from the adversary. Those who hate us take plunder for themselves.
Kiswahili: Umetufanya turudi nyuma mbele ya adui, nao watesi wetu wametuteka nyara.
Ekegusii: Gwatokorire gotama ababisa baito, na barabwo babeire bagosakora ebinto biaito.

English: But the tax collector stood at a distance. He bowed his head and prayed, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
Ekegusii: Galatians 5:22

English: They answered Jesus, and said, “We don’t know.” He also said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo wakamjibu Yesu, “Sisi hatujui.” Naye akawaambia, “Wala mimi sitawaambia ni kwa mamlaka gani ninatenda mambo haya.”
Ekegusii: Bakamoiraneria, “Titomanyeti.” Ere akabateebia, “Nonya ninche tinkobateebia inwe nase kobua ki ngokora aya.

English: You were the anointed cherub who covers. Then I set you up on the holy mountain of God. You have walked up and down in the middle of the stones of fire.
Kiswahili: Ulitiwa mafuta kuwa kerubi mlinzi, kwa kuwa hivyo ndivyo nilivyokuweka wakfu. Ulikuwa kwenye mlima mtakatifu wa Mungu; ulitembea katikati ya vito vya moto.
Ekegusii: Aye nigo kwarenge egetongwa kebwate chimbaba oagetwe amaguta, ogatuba oboagare obonene. Inche nigo nakobegete ase egetunwa egechenu kia Nyasae, agwo ase kwarenge kona‐gotaara ase egati y’amagena are nomorero.

English: In the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no kind of work shall be done in them, except that which every man must eat, only that may be done by you.
Kiswahili: Katika siku ya kwanza mtakuwa na kusanyiko takatifu, na kusanyiko jingine katika siku ya saba. Katika siku hizo msifanye kazi kamwe isipokuwa kutayarisha chakula cha kila mmoja; hilo ndilo tu mtakalofanya.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko rie ritang’ani inamobe nomosangererekano bwatananire ase ogosasiima, na ase rituko ria gatano na kabere boigo mobe nomosangererekano bwatananire ase ogosasiima. Ase amatuko ayio timokora meremo ende yonsi, otatiga okoroisia endagera ase kera omonto ayio oka naro morakore.

English: In the day that he goes into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin offering,” says the Lord Yahweh.
Kiswahili: Siku atakapoingia katika ukumbi wa ndani wa mahali patakatifu ili kuhudumu, atatoa sadaka ya dhambi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe, asema Bwana Mwenyezi.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko riria arasoe ase eraaro ya ime ase obokoreri bwaye agwo Aase Aachenu, goika arue ekeng’wanso kiaye ki’ebibe. Nabo Omonene ateebire.

English: The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland.
Kiswahili: Mfalme akafanya fedha kuwa kitu cha kawaida kama mawe huko Yerusalemu, mierezi akaifanya kuwa mingi kama mikuyu vilimani.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akarenta chifeta chinyinge agwo Yerusalemu, chikabucha buna amagena, ne chibao chi’emecharake chiarenge chinyinge buna echi’emeko yarenge ase ense omweya.

Kiswahili: Ni nani huyu anayekuja kutoka Edomu, kutoka Bosra, mwenye mavazi yaliyotiwa madoa mekundu? Ni nani huyu, aliyevikwa joho la kifahari, anayetembea kwa ukuu wa nguvu zake? “Mimi ndimi, nisemaye katika haki, mwenye nguvu wa kuokoa.”

Kiswahili: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo wakaja ili kumjaribu kwa kumuuliza, “Je, ni halali mtu kumwacha mke wake?”

Kiswahili: “Mwanadamu, uelekeze uso wako upande wa kusini, hubiri juu ya upande wa kusini na utoe unabii juu ya msitu wa Negebu.
Ekegusii: “Aye Mwanyabaanto, rigereria gochia ensemo ya Irianyi, oyerarerie ring’ana rire mamincha yaye, na obaane igoro ye rinani ri’ense ya Negebu.

English: Last year, we remembered things that pleased God very much. This year, let us work hard. Are you well? Good. Are you still alive? Very well. Remember this thing. That is it. Let us give thanks to God very much.
Ekegusii: Last year, ntwabarete ebinto biragere otebie Omonene Nyasae buna mbuya mono. This year, kobara tikoiyo. Nkwaboka bono rimaambia? Good. Nkoeyana ore still? Buya sana. Tigera igo bono. That is it. Bono rirorio gaki, tebia Omonene Nyasae buna mbuya mono.

English: Long ago, years and years, my grandfather went to visit his friend in Cairo. That grandfather I remember very well. Very well he told stories, making people want to listen to him, so they would gather around him.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, omoremi oyomo narengeo ase ekenyoro kia Makairo. Bono omoremi oyo natugete esese. Esese eye nigo yarenge engiya, goikera akayetigire yoka korenda omochi oye, ekero akogenda aande.

English: You have said to me, Lord Yahweh, ‘Buy the field for money, and call witnesses;’ whereas the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.”
Kiswahili: Ingawa mji utatiwa mikononi mwa Wakaldayo, wewe, Ee Bwana Mwenyezi, uliniambia, ‘Nunua shamba kwa fedha, na jambo hilo lishuhudiwe.’ ”

Kiswahili: Matukio mengine ya utawala wa Amoni na yale aliyoyafanya, je, hayakuandikwa katika kitabu cha kumbukumbu za wafalme wa Yuda?

English: [III]. The diviners [The leader Manyanta who was also a warrior]. They say that the Abanyaribari and the Abamachoge were also diviners. The Gusii people remember them fondly, remembering their wisdom and knowledge. The leader Manyanta was particularly skilled in dealing with the Abanyaribari and the Abamachoge.
Ekegusii: [II]. Abasweta [ Omogaka Manyanta nere orenge omorai]. Ka moranche inyora buna Abanyaribari amo na Abamachoge nabwo Abasweta. Abagusii mbebagete amarieta gete ye chingiti ao ao, amarieta ayio akabwata. Omogaka Manyanta nigo arenge koraaa Abanyaribari amo na Abamachoge bonsi.

English: Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
Kiswahili: Mose akawachagua watu wenye uwezo kutoka Israeli yote, akawafanya kuwa viongozi wa watu, maafisa juu ya maelfu, mamia, hamsini na makumi.

English: Hushai said to Absalom, “The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good.”
Kiswahili: Hushai akamjibu Absalomu, “Shauri la Ahithofeli alilotoa halifai kwa wakati huu.

Kiswahili: Alitia nakshi za makerubi, simba na miti ya mitende juu ya uso wa vishikio na juu ya papi, katika kila nafasi iliyopatikana, pamoja na mataji yaliyosokotwa kuzunguka pande zote.

Kiswahili: Walimwaga damu isiyo na hatia, damu za wana wao na binti zao, ambao waliwatoa dhabihu kwa sanamu za Kanaani, nayo nchi ikanajisika kwa damu zao.

Kiswahili: Lakini watawala wa mwanzoni, wale walionitangulia, waliwalemea watu na kuchukua kutoka kwao shekeli arobaini za fedha, pamoja na chakula na mvinyo. Wasaidizi wao pia walijifanya wakuu juu ya watu. Lakini kwa kumheshimu Mungu sikufanya hivyo.

Ekegusii: Ekerengererio ki’abaonto abariri nigo kere ang’e n’emenwa yabo, korende eki bagoteeba abanyene chisemi nigo gekorwa ase ebirengererio biabo.

English: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
Kiswahili: Sasa nanyi mmethibitika kwamba hamna msaada wowote; mnaona jambo la kutisha, nanyi mnaogopa.
Ekegusii: Nabogio nainwe mwabeire ase ’nde buna chintuboka chiria; mwarorire emechando yane, mwakumirie na kwoboa.

English: but you said, “No, for we will flee on horses;” therefore you will flee; and, “We will ride on the swift;” therefore those who pursue you will be swift.
Kiswahili: Mlisema, ‘Hapana, tutakimbia kwa farasi.’ Kwa hiyo mtakimbia! Mlisema, ‘Tutakimbia kwa farasi waendao kasi.’ Kwa hiyo wanaowafukuza watakwenda kasi!
Ekegusii: Nigo mogoteeba ng’a moriine chibarasi chikominyoka mono, motame. Ee, goika motame. Inwe moganetie gotama ne chibarasi chinyango, korende ababisa baino abwo bakobabwatia nigo bare abaminyoki kobabua.

English: and tell Tyre, ‘You who dwell at the entry of the sea, who are the merchant of the peoples to many islands, the Lord Yahweh says: “You, Tyre, have said, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’
Kiswahili: Umwambie Tiro, ulioko kwenye lango la bahari, ufanyao biashara na mataifa mengi ya pwani, ‘Hili ndilo Bwana Mwenyezi asemalo: “ ‘Ee Tiro, wewe umesema, “Mimi ni mkamilifu katika uzuri.”
Ekegusii: Otebie Turo oyio ore ase egesoero ki’enyancha, naende ogokora oboonchoreria nabaanto abange bamenyete ase chinse chire ang’e nenyancha: Aya naro Omonene agoteeba: Aye Turo, nigo ogokwana ng’a nigo ore omoseera omoikeranu.

English: He answered Arioch the king’s captain, “Why is the decree so urgent from the king?” Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
Kiswahili: Akamuuliza huyo afisa wa mfalme, “Kwa nini mfalme ametoa amri kali hivyo?” Ndipo Arioko akamweleza Danieli jambo hilo.
Ekegusii: akamobooria, “Nase ki omorwoti arure ogochika ogotindi iga?” Erio Arioki agateebia Danieli amang’ana onsi.

English: Yahweh said to Moses, “Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo Bwana akamwambia Mose, “Mchukue Yoshua mwana wa Nuni, mtu ambaye Roho yuko ndani yake, uweke mkono juu yake.
Ekegusii: Omonene agateebia Musa, “Ira Yoshua, mosinto o Nuni, omonto oyio omoika one ore ime yaye, erio omobekere amaboko.

English: It will come to pass in that day, says Yahweh of Armies, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds. Strangers will no more make them their bondservants;
Kiswahili: “ ‘Katika siku ile,’ asema Bwana Mwenye Nguvu Zote, ‘nitaivunja nira kutoka shingoni mwao na kuvipasua vifungo vyao; wageni hawatawafanya tena watumwa.
Ekegusii: Omonene bw’Emeganda nigo agoteeba iga: “Nebe ekero rituko riria riraike, nimbune amakorogoto, ninyerusie ase amagoti abo. Nimbasansore chingataare basibeire, na barabwo tibakoba abasomba b’abaanto b’egesaku ekeao nonya ng’ake.

English: Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord.
Kiswahili: Naye Maria akasema: “Moyo wangu wamwadhimisha Bwana,
Ekegusii: Mariamu agateeba, “Omoyo one otogirie Omonene,

English: They traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around them, and they didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.
Kiswahili: Kisha wakaondoka, na hofu ya Mungu ikawapata miji yote iliyowazunguka. Kwa hiyo hakuna aliyewafuatia wana wa Yakobo.
Ekegusii: Ekero baimogete kogenda orogendo rwabo, okoondokia gokarua ase Nyasae, gokabwata abanto b’emechie eria yabaetanaine; Ase igo tibanyara komonyookia basinto ba Yakobo.

English: Then the king said to him, “Don’t you think that Bel is a living god? Don’t you see how much he eats and drinks every day?”
Ekegusii: Erio omorwoti akamobooria, aye nigo okagete buna Beli tari Nyasae bw’ekeene? Aye torochi buna akoragera na konywa ase kera rituko?

English: It will happen, when many evils and troubles have come on them, that this song will testify before them as a witness; for it will not be forgotten out of the mouths of their descendants; for I know their ways and what they are doing today, before I have brought them into the land which I promised them.”
Kiswahili: Maafa na shida zitakapokuja juu yao, wimbo huu utashuhudia dhidi yao, kwa sababu hautasahauliwa na wazao wao. Ninajua lile wanaloandaa kufanya, hata kabla sijawaingiza katika nchi niliyowaahidi kwa kiapo.”
Ekegusii: Ekero amabe amaange na emechando biraabe bikobaachera, ogoteera oko ’nakoborokererie na kobe kirori ase bare, ekiagera tigokwebwa nonya nase chinderia chiabo. Nimanyete ebirengererio bare nabio bono, ritang’ani konya ntarabarenta ase ense eyio nariete eira ng’a nimbayee.”

English: For you see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;
Kiswahili: Ndugu zangu, kumbukeni mlivyokuwa mlipoitwa. Kwa kipimo cha kibinadamu, si wengi wenu mliokuwa na hekima. Si wengi mliokuwa na ushawishi, si wengi mliozaliwa katika jamaa zenye vyeo.
Ekegusii: Naki baminto, rengereria nabaanto b’engencho ki more aba Nyasae arangeirie; tari abange ase more bare nobong’aini bwa Mwanyabaanto, tari abange bare ne chinguru, tari abange baiboretwe nobonene.

English: God crosses hands. Key verse Genesis 48:13,14 Jacob embraced them placing his hands on their heads Ephraim and Manasseh. God embraced him placing his hands on the heads of Jacob and Esau, Genesis 25:23. Let us remember this […]
Ekegusii: God crosses hands. Key verse Genesis 48:13,14 Jacob ogokorekani amaboko chingaki are gosesenia Ephraim na Manase. Nyasae ingokorekani are amaboko chingaki agosesenia Jacob na Esau, Genesis 25:23. Amegerio tokonyora naria […]

English: You have also given me the shield of your salvation. Your gentleness has made me great.
Kiswahili: Hunipa ngao yako ya ushindi, unajishusha chini ili kuniinua.
Ekegusii: “Aye kwang’eire enguba yao ase ogontooria, na ogokonywa kwao gwankorire nabeire omonene.

English: Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down, likewise also of the fish as much as they desired.
Kiswahili: Ndipo Yesu akachukua ile mikate, akamshukuru Mungu na kuwagawia wale watu waliokuwa wameketi. Akafanya vivyo hivyo na wale samaki. Kila mtu akapata kadiri alivyotaka.
Ekegusii: Yeso akabogoria emegati; kayesesenirie, akagabera abaikaransete; naboigo ne chinswe chiria, koreng’ana buna barigetie.

English: and that in me and my brothers you may bring to an end the wrath of the Almighty which has been justly brought upon our whole race.”
Ekegusii: Nigo ngosaba buna inche n’abamura baminto tobe ab’omoerio konyora egesusuro kia Nyasae ekio ase ekeene kianyorire ense yaito yonsi.

English: All the offering shall be a square of twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. You shall offer it as a holy offering, with the possession of the city.
Kiswahili: Eneo lote la hiyo sehemu litakuwa mraba, yaani, dhiraa 25,000 kila upande. Kama toleo maalum mtatenga sehemu takatifu, pamoja na milki ya mji.
Ekegusii: Orogongo roria rwonsi oroochenu nigo rorabe orw’ekerengo gie chimoti chilifu emerongo ebere na isano (25,000), chinsemo chionsi nigo chirabe chireng’aine. Oro narwo orogongo oroochenu amo norw’omochie oyio.

English: And because of this matter which caused great trouble, it wasn’t decided that the elders of Gusii should meet in Kisumu and discuss things and agree. Orechi did not allow it until he achieved his goal. That is why it was decided that Gusii would not have anything to do with this story and its consequences because it was troublesome.
Ekegusii: Ase okogenderera n' omogano oyo oito, nigo togotebigwa buna abamura ba Mogusii baria banganyete korwa Egesumu nigo barenge batano na babere. Orechi ere tari gokwanwa ase achiete. Bono nigo togotebigwa ng'a Mogusii narenge ne chinyomba isano na ibere buna ekobwatia.

English: National Coordinating Committee affirming Kenya's pledges on food system reform, nutrition financing, and wellness pathways.
Kiswahili: Kamati ya Kitaifa ya Uratibu ikithibitisha ahadi za Kenya kuhusu mageuzi ya mfumo wa chakula, ufadhili wa lishe, na njia za ustawi.

Kiswahili: Maafisa wa afya ya umma wa @MOH_Kenya leo wametekeleza zoezi kubwa la ufukizaji na kuua vijidudu huko Kawangware ili kuzuia kuenea kwa #COVID19 kwa jamii. Hivi sasa, eneo hilo lina kesi 20 chanya. #KomeshaCorona

English: And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work and will preserve me for his heavenly Kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Kiswahili: Bwana ataniokoa katika kila shambulio baya na kunileta salama katika Ufalme wake wa mbinguni. Atukuzwe yeye milele na milele. Amen.
Ekegusii: Omonene nansibore korwa ase amabe onsi, na antoorie goika nsoe ase oborwoti bwa igoro. Ogotogigwa nokwaye kare na kare. Amina.

English: TAKING STOCK OF DEVOLUTION President Kenyatta urges the National Government and county governments to work together to address climate change in Kenya
Kiswahili: KUCHUNGUZA UADILIFU Rais Kenyatta ahimiza Serikali ya Kitaifa na serikali za kaunti kufanya kazi pamoja ili kushughulikia mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa nchini Kenya
Ekegusii: Korigereria ayare anyarekanire inse yechikaunti omonene bw'ense Kenyatta orure okoboria ase eserekari enene nechiserekari chie chikaunti kobwaterana ase okorenda ebitoetanaine ako noboonchoreria bwerire.

English: By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively.
Kiswahili: Ili kunizuia nisijivune kwa sababu ya ufunuo huu mkuu, nilipewa mwiba katika mwili wangu, mjumbe wa Shetani, ili anitese.
Ekegusii: Erinde timbaisa gocha koenena goetania ekerengo, ekiagera ase obonge bw’okomaanorerwa okwo, nkaegwa riigwa rimbetete ase omobere, omotomwa o Saitani, ang’ake, timbaisa gocha koenena goetania ekerengo.

English: Reward those who wait for you, and men will put their trust in your prophets.
Ekegusii: Obae ebiegwa biao kwaroberetie korwa omochakano na tiga ababani bao baegwe amasikani.

English: They cried aloud, and cut themselves in their way with knives and lances until the blood gushed out on them.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo wakapiga kelele zaidi na kama ilivyokuwa desturi yao wakajichanja wenyewe kwa visu na vyembe, mpaka damu ikachuruzika.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio bagaaka eriogi rinene, bagekebia emeyio ne chinsara chi’amatimo, buna engencho yabo yarenge, goika amanyinga agacharaara korwa ase emebere yabo.

English: Governor James Ongwae has signed the Finance Bill for the fiscal year 2020/2021
Ekegusii: Ongwae obekire esei omoswada bwechibesa bwomwaka 2020/2021

English: But as for the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel burned none of them, except Hazor only. Joshua burned that.
Kiswahili: Lakini Israeli hawakuichoma moto hata mojawapo ya miji iliyojengwa katika vilima vyao vidogo isipokuwa mji wa Hazori ambao Yoshua aliuchoma moto.
Ekegusii: Abaisraeli tibasambete emechie eyio yaagachetwe ase ebigoro igoro, otatiga Hazori bwoka, noro Yoshua asambete.

English: On the twelfth day Ahira the son of Enan, prince of the children of Naphtali,
Kiswahili: Siku ya kumi na mbili Ahira mwana wa Enani, kiongozi wa watu wa Naftali, alileta sadaka yake.
Ekegusii: Rituko ria ikomi na kabere Ahira, mosinto o Enani bw’egesaku kia Nafutali, akarenta okoruegwa kwaye.

English: I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers,
Kiswahili: Siku zote ninamshukuru Mungu ninapokukumbuka katika maombi yangu,
Ekegusii: Oyominto Filemoni, ase ogosaba kwane botambe nigo ngoakera Nyasae one ng’a mbuya mono ekero ngokoinyora.

English: Postpartum women should take deworming medication to improve nutrition and milk quality.
Kiswahili: Wanawake baada ya kujifungua wanapaswa kutumia dawa za minyoo ili kuboresha lishe na ubora wa maziwa.
Ekegusii: Abakungu mbabwenerete gotumeka amariogo yogoita ebianda ekero baiboire nario barakongie endagera n'obuya bw'amabere.

English: The wine press was trodden outside of the city, and blood came out of the wine press, up to the bridles of the horses, as far as one thousand six hundred stadia.
Kiswahili: Lile shinikizo likakanyagwa nje ya mji, nayo damu ikatiririka kama mafuriko kutoka hilo shinikizo kufikia kimo cha hatamu za farasi, kwa umbali wa maili 200.
Ekegusii: Na ekemitero keria kegatiringwa isiko y’omochie, na amanyinga agaiteka korwa ase ekemitero, na amanyinga aria akagenda ase oboare bwe chimaeli amagana abere, agaichora goika ebiokio bie chibarasi.

English: Don’t enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous.
Kiswahili: Usimhukumu mtumishi wako, kwa kuwa hakuna mtu anayeishi aliye mwenye haki mbele zako.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kong’ira inche omosomba oo ase ekegambero, ekiagera ase abwo bare moyo onde tari ore omooronge asore.

English: For this is not the first day wherein your wisdom is manifested; but from the beginning of your days all the people have known your understanding, because the disposition of your heart is good.
Ekegusii: Rituko ria reero tari rirorio ritang’ani kworokia obong’aini bwao. Intwe ntokomanyete korwa ase obwana bwao buna omonto omonyaseemi na obwate enkoro endemu.

English: I have also made a decree that whoever alters this message, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and fastened on it; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.
Kiswahili: Zaidi ya hayo, ninaamuru kwamba mtu yeyote atakayebadilisha amri hii, boriti itangʼolewa kutoka nyumba yake, ichongwe upande mmoja na atumbuliwe nayo. Kwa ajili ya kosa hili nyumba yake ifanywe lundo la taka.
Ekegusii: Boigo nachiikire ng’a, monto onde bwensi oraonchore ring’ana eri, omwamba osomorwe korwa ase enyomba yaye, na ere omonyene atongwe ase oro, na enyomba yaye ekorwe ebe etui y’eubi.

English: And Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June 22, 2011.
Ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi (June) 22, 2011.

English: However, I also want to remember what the elder taught me about this history. Because of this, I will try to explain the importance of this history to the Gusii people. The elder said that work should be done properly, and the land of Nyabarati should not be compared to cattle.
Ekegusii: Nonye niche nigo neyagia omotwe ekero omogaka antebia omobayeno oyo. Bono nche nigo naboria sokoro angoorobererie aake, erinde nario ndamanye eng'encho y' omobayeno oyo bwa Abagusii. Bono omogaka nigo ateba buna korwa kare kare, omokungu obande nigo arenge kobwekanigwa n' eng'ombe nyabarati.

English: “When the children of your people speak to you, saying, ‘Won’t you show us what you mean by these?’
Kiswahili: “Watu wako watakapokuuliza, ‘Je, hutatuambia ni nini maana ya jambo hili?’
Ekegusii: Ekero abanto bamino barakoborie iga: Inee! Nototeebie engencho gwakorera iga?

English: For I have kept the ways of Yahweh, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana nimezishika njia za Bwana; sijatenda ubaya nikamwacha Mungu wangu.
Ekegusii: Inche nabeire nkobwatia chinchera chia Omonene, tintigeti Nyasae one ase ogokora obonyaka.

English: For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana viumbe vyote vinangoja kwa shauku kudhihirishwa kwa watoto wa Mungu.
Ekegusii: Nabo ebitongwa bionsi nigo biganyete n’okogania okonene mono ase rituko riria Abana ba Nyasae bagocha koorokigwa.

English: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana lazima Kristo atawale mpaka awe amewaweka adui zake wote chini ya miguu yake.
Ekegusii: Naki negwenerete ere agambe, goika abeeke ababisa bonsi inse ase amagoro aye.

English: But Yahweh’s angel didn’t appear to Manoah or to his wife any more. Then Manoah knew that he was Yahweh’s angel.
Kiswahili: Malaika wa Bwana hakumtokea tena Manoa na mkewe. Ndipo Manoa akatambua kuwa huyo alikuwa malaika wa Bwana.
Ekegusii: Korwa ekero keria omomalaika oria taoroka ase Manoa naende, gose ase omorugi oye, Erio Manoa akamanya ng’a oria nigo arenge omomalaika bw’Omonene.

English: of the gods of the peoples who are around you, near to you, or far off from you, from the one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth—
Kiswahili: miungu ya watu wanaowazunguka, ikiwa karibu au mbali, kutoka mwisho mmoja wa nchi mpaka mwingine),
Ekegusii: Oyomo obo nanyaare gokoebereria osasiime chinyasae chinde chi’ abanto abwo bagoetanaine, bamenyete aare korwa ase ore, gose ang’e, korwa ensinyo eyemo y’ense goika eyende.

English: He said, “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid. Peace be to you. Be strong. Yes, be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”
Kiswahili: Akasema, “Ee mtu upendwaye sana, usiogope. Amani iwe kwako! Uwe na nguvu sasa; jipe nguvu.” Alipozungumza nami, nilipata nguvu, nikasema, “Nena, bwana wangu, kwa kuwa umenipa nguvu.”
Ekegusii: aganteebia, “Aye omonto bwanchire mono, tibwoboa, omorembe obe amo naye! Tenena bokong’u, naende obe omoremu!” Ekero arenge gokwana nainche, nkanyora chinguru, nkamotebia, “Aye Omonene one, kwana, ekiagera kwambekeire chinguru!”

English: But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.”
Kiswahili: Lakini hata ikiwa hatatuokoa, ee mfalme, tunataka ufahamu kwamba, hatutaitumikia miungu yako wala kuiabudu sanamu ya dhahabu uliyoisimamisha.”
Ekegusii: Korende nonya tagochia gototooria korwa ase ore aye omorwoti, goika omanye ng’a intwe titogwancha gokorera chinyasae chiao, gose gosasiima omogwekano bw’etaabu, oyio gwatenenetie.”

English: For from garments comes a moth, and from a woman comes a woman’s wickedness.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera esukubi nigo egosoka korwa ime yechianga, na obobe bw’omokuungu nigo bokorwa ase omokungu.

English: The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
Kiswahili: Adamu na mkewe wote wawili walikuwa uchi, wala hawakuona aibu.
Ekegusii: Omosacha na omokungu nigo baarenge getirianda, na tibaare kororerana obosooku.

English: Indeed a man shall take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying, “You have clothing, you be our ruler, and let this ruin be under your hand.”
Kiswahili: Mtu atamkamata mmoja wa ndugu zake katika nyumba ya baba yake na kusema, “Unalo joho, sasa uwe kiongozi wetu, tawala lundo hili la magofu!”
Ekegusii: Engaki eyio omonto nabwate oyomwabo baiboire komo amoteebie, “Aye nobwate chianga okobeeka, ase ayio kabe omogambi oito, otenenere obogaambi obo bwanyegerigwe.”

English: Let's gather together, let's pray to God to protect us with the life of Kate
Ekegusii: Togotenga tokore,twende tosabe Nyasaye atosesenie na obogima bwa Kate

English: For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are far off, even as many as the Lord our God will call to himself.”
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa ahadi hii ni kwa ajili yenu na watoto wenu, na kwa wote walio mbali, na kila mtu ambaye Bwana Mungu wetu atamwita amjie.”
Ekegusii: Naki eira eye nigo ere ase more na ase abana baino, na ase abanto bonsi abare aare, na bonsi abarangerigwe n’Omonene nyasae oito.”

English: He will sharpen stern wrath for a sword. The universe will go with him to fight against his frenzied foes.
Ekegusii: Natieri endamwamu yaye enene buna omoro, na ense yonsi nebwaterane nere korwania ababisa abwo batabwati semi.

English: This is the third time I am coming to you. “At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.”
Kiswahili: Hii ndiyo mara ya tatu mimi kuja kwenu. “Shtaka lolote lazima lithibitishwe na mashahidi wawili au watatu.”
Ekegusii: Ekero eke nekia gatato ngocha ase more. Ase emenwa y’abarori babere gose batato kera ring’ana nariikeranigwe.

English: Come to her with all your soul. Keep her ways with your whole power.
Ekegusii: Mochiere ere chisemi n’omoyo oo bwonsi, na kobwatia ebirage biaye n’echinguru chiao chionsi.

English: I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
Kiswahili: Sijaziacha amri zilizotoka midomoni mwake; nimeyathamini maneno ya kinywa chake kuliko chakula changu cha kila siku.
Ekegusii: Tinana gotiga kobwata amachiiko akwanete; nimbwatetie amang’ana ere akwanete, gose tari aya naroberetie inche omonyene.

English: Mordecai established it, and the Jews took upon themselves, upon their offspring, and upon those who were joined to them to observe it, neither would they on any account behave differently; but these days were to be a memorial kept in every generation, city, family, and province.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Esiteri achete ase omorwoti na komoteebia amang’ana ayio, Omorwoti akarua ogochika ase amarube ng’a omoroberio oria Hamani akorete mamincha y’Abayahudi omoiraneire ere omonyene, na ere na abamura baye bagatongwa ase chimbambo igoro.

English: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is their poverty.
Kiswahili: Mali ya tajiri ni mji wake wenye ngome, bali ufukara ni maangamizi ya maskini.
Ekegusii: Obotenenku bw’omonto omonda nigo bore ase are buna omochie ogiteire chindwaki, korende obotaka nabwo ogosirigwa kw’abataka.

English: The following is a copy of the letter containing orders: The great King Ahasuerus sends greetings to the rulers of provinces in one hundred twenty-seven local governance regions, from India to Ethiopia, even to those who are faithful to our interests. Many who have been frequently honored by the most abundant kindness of their benefactors have conceived ambitious designs, and not only endeavor to hurt our subjects, but moreover, not being able to bear prosperity, they also endeavor to plot against their own benefactors. They not only would utterly abolish gratitude from among men, but also, elated by the boastings of men who are strangers to all that is good, they supposed that they would escape the sin-hating vengeance of the ever-seeing God. And oftentimes evil exhortation has made partakers of the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and has involved in irremediable calamities many of those who had been appointed to offices of authority, who had been entrusted with the management of their friends’ affairs; while men, by the false sophistry of an evil disposition, have deceived the simple goodwill of the ruling powers. And it is possible to see this, not so much from more ancient traditional accounts, as it is immediately in your power to see it by examining what things have been wickedly perpetrated by the baseness of men unworthily holding power. It is right to take heed with regard to the future, that we may maintain the government in undisturbed peace for all men, adopting needful changes, and ever judging those cases which come under our notice with truly equitable decisions. For whereas Haman, a Macedonian, the son of Hammedatha, in reality an alien from the blood of the Persians, and differing widely from our mild course of government, having been hospitably entertained by us, obtained so large a share of our universal kindness as to be called our father, and to continue the person next to the royal throne, reverenced of all; he however, overcome by pride, endeavored to deprive us of our dominion, and our life; having by various and subtle artifices demanded for destruction both Mordecai our deliverer and perpetual benefactor, and Esther the blameless consort of our kingdom, along with their whole nation. For by these methods he thought, having surprised us in a defenseless state, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians. But we find that the Jews, who have been consigned to destruction by the most abominable of men, are not malefactors, but living according to the most just laws, and being the sons of the living God, the most high and mighty, who maintains the kingdom, to us as well as to our forefathers, in the most excellent order. You will therefore do well in refusing to obey the letter sent by Haman the son of Hammedatha, because he who has done these things has been hanged with his whole family at the gates of Susa, Almighty God having swiftly returned to him a worthy punishment. We enjoin you then, having openly published a copy of this letter in every place, to give the Jews permission to use their own lawful customs and to strengthen them, that on the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, on the self-same day, they may defend themselves against those who attack them in a time of affliction. For in the place of the destruction of the chosen race, Almighty God has granted them this time of gladness. Therefore you also, among your notable feasts, must keep a distinct day with all festivity, that both now and hereafter it may be a day of deliverance to us and who are well disposed toward the Persians, but to those that plotted against us a memorial of destruction. And every city and province collectively, which shall not do accordingly, shall be consumed with vengeance by spear and fire. It shall be made not only inaccessible to men, but most hateful to wild beasts and birds forever. Let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom. Let all the Jews be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies.

English: 1 Now there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 2 Near the Sheep Gate there is a pool called Bethesda, which has five porticoes. 3 Here lay a great number of people who were sick—blind, lame, paralyzed—waiting for the water to be stirred. 4 An angel would come down and stir the water, and whoever went in first would be healed. 5 One man was lying there who had been ill for thirty-eight years. 6 When Jesus saw him lying there and knew he had been there a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to get well?” 7 The sick man answered, “Sir, I have no one to help me get into the pool when the water is stirred. By the time I get there, someone else goes down ahead of me.” 8 Jesus told him, “Get up! Pick up your mat and walk.” 9 At once the man was cured; he picked up his mat and began to walk. 10 It was the Sabbath day when this happened. 11 So the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “It is against our law for you to carry your mat on the Sabbath.” 12 He replied, “The man who made me well said to me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’” 13 They asked him, “Who is this who told you to pick it up and walk?” 14 Later Jesus found him at the temple and said to him, “See, you are well again. Stop sinning or something worse may happen to you.” 15 The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. 16 Because of this, the Jews persecuted Jesus and tried to kill him because he did such things on the Sabbath. 17 But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, and I also am working.” 18 For this reason the Jews tried all the more to kill him, because not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was also calling God his Father, making himself equal to God. 19 Then Jesus explained, “Very truly I tell you, the Son can do nothing by himself; he can do only what he sees his Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does also. 20 For the Father loves the Son and shows him all he does. Yes, and he will show him even greater works than these. 21 All those the Father gives me will come to me, and I will never reject anyone who comes to me. 22 For I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but to do the will of the one who sent me. 23 And this is the will of the one who sent me—that everyone who believes in me should have eternal life, and I shall raise them up on the last day.” 24 Very truly I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life now. 25 Very truly I tell you, a time is coming and has already arrived when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. 26 For just as the Father has life within himself, so he has granted the Son to have life within himself. 27 And he has given him authority to judge because he is the Son of Man. 28 So do not be surprised at my saying, “You must be born again.” 29 The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” 30 “We know that you are a teacher come from God,” they replied. 31 Jesus answered, “Believe in me! If you believe, you will know that I am in my Father and my Father is in me.” 32 “These words I am saying to you are not just my own. Rather, it is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work. 33 Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on the evidence of the works I have done. 34 I tell you the truth, whoever believes in me will do the same works I have done, and even greater ones. 35 Because I am going to the Father, and you will see me no longer. 36 Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father.” 37 Jesus answered, “Don’t you know me, Philip, even after I have been among you such a long time? Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? 38 Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you are not just my own. Rather, it is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work. 39 Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on the evidence of the works I have done. 40 Don’t you believe that I am in the Father and that the Father is in me? 41 I tell you the truth, whoever believes in me will do the same works I have done, and even greater ones. 42 Do you believe that I am in the Father and that the Father is in me? 43 I have told you this, so that when it happens, you will believe. 44 But when the Helper comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who goes out from the Father—he will testify about me. 45 And I tell you the truth, whoever believes in me will also do what I have done. Indeed, they will do greater things, because I am going to the Father. 46 If you ask something of my Father in my name, he will give it to you. 47 Yet you don’t ask me anything.
Ekegusii: 1 Nyuma as'aya ndiarenge rituko rinene ri'Abayahudi; Yesu agatira kogenda Yerusalemu. 2 Naende aria Yerusalemu as'egesieri kie ching'ondi ndiarenge ritibo rikorokwa as'Ekeibirania Bethesaida, narirorio mbiarengeo ebisoero bitano. 3 Ime as'ebio mbarenge abanto abange abarwaire bakorara, emeuko, chirema, ab'ebimo biabo biomire, baganyete amache aseroke. 4 Naki ekero gete rilaika ngoika riarenge riasoa ase riria ritibo, koyaturubania amache: nabo ere oyore gosoa ritang'ani nyuma as'amache agoturubanigwa, igare kogwena oborwaire bwonsi obwamonyorete. 5 Narenge aroro omonto gete oyorenge noborwaire bw'emiaka emerongo etato netano netato. 6 Yesu agachia komorora oyio oraire, akamanya ng'a obaire engecho eye amatuko amange, akamotebia, Norigetie koba omogima? 7 Oria omorwaire akamoiraneria, Omonene, tindi nomonto okombeka ritibo ime, amache gagoturubanigwa: korende ekero ngochicha inche, omonto onde osoa ritang'ani asende. 8 Yesu akamotebia, Tenena, etweke egesero kiao, ogende. 9 Erio kegima omonto oria akaba omogima, agetweka egesero kiaye, akagenda. Nabo yarenge esabato rituko riria. 10 Abayahudi bakamotebia oria okonyetwe, Rero nesnbato, tari boronge asore gwetweka egesero kiao. 11 Akabairaneria, Ere oyonkora koba omogima nere ontebia, Etweke egesero kiao, ogende. 12 Bakamoboria, Oria ogotebia, Etweke egesero kiao ogende, ning'o? 13 Korende oria ogwenetigwe tamomanyete gose ning'o: naki Yesu erusananetie, ekiagera barenge abanto abange aas'aria. 14 Nyuma as'aya Yesu akamonyora hekalu itne, akamotebia, Rora, kwabaire omogima: tokora ebibe naende, ring'ana rire ribe kobua tiricha gokonyora. 15 Oria omonto akagenda, akabatebia Abayahudi amang'ana ng'a Yesu nere onkorete nkaba omogima. 16 As'ayio Abayahudi bagachaka komochanda Yesu, bakarigia komoita, ekiagera akora aya rituko ri'esabato. 17 Yesu akabairaneria, Tata one ngokorare emeremo nonya ngoika bono, nainche ngokorande emeremo. 18 Nabo ekiagera as'aya Abayahudi bakamenta korigia komoita, ekiagera atasareti esabato yoka, korende amo naya namorogete Nyasaye Tata oye, ogwekora koreng'ana buna Nyasaye. 19 Yesu akairaneria, akabatebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nabatebirie, Omwana takonyara gokora ring'ana ere bweka, tatiga riria amororire Tata agokora: naki onsi agokora ere ayio naio n'Omwana agokora, 20 Naki Tata amwanchire Omwana, okomworokia onsi ayagokora omonyene: nemeremo emenene kobua eyeiga namworokie erinde inwe monyare gokumia. 21 Naki buna Tata akobibokia ebitondo nakobia obogima, naboigo n'Omwana akobaa obogima abarigetie. 22 Ekiagera Tata tari komogambia omonto onde bwonsi, korende omoire Omwana okogamba gwonsi; 23 erinde bonsi bamosike Omwana, buna bamosigete Tata. Oyotamosigeti Omwana tamosigeti Tata omotomete, 24 Ekeene, ekeene, nabatebirie, oyokoigwa ring'ana riane, nakomwancha ere oyontomete nare nobogima bwa kare nakare, gose tagoika as'ekina, korende oetire korwa as'amakweri goika as'obogima. 25 Ekeene, ekeene, nabatebirie, Ensa ngochere, nabono nere, ebitondo biraigwe eriogi ri'Omwana o Nyasaye; nabaria bakorigwa nababe moyo. 26 Naki buna Tata are nobogima ime yaye omonyene; naboigo omoeire n'Omwana koba nobogima ime yaye omonyene: 27 akamoa okobua kw'ogokora ekina ekiagera ere n'Omwana-o-mwanyabanto. 28 Timokumia as'aya: naki ensa ngochere, ekero abanto bonsi bare ase chimbera ime baraigwe eriogi riaye, 29 nabarabwo nabasoke; baria abare gokora amaya as'okobokigwa kw'obogima; nabaria abakorire amabe as'okobokigwa gw'ekina. 30 Inche omonyene tinkonyara gokora kende gionsi: buna nkoigwa, nabo nkogamba: nekina kiane iga kere boronge; ekiagera tindi koborigia obwanchani bwane, korende nobwanchani bwaye Tata oyontomete. 31 Inche kondetebe omonyene, ogoteba kwane tari okw'ekeene. 32 Nare oyonde oyokombera kirori; nainche namanyire ng'a oborori bwaye agonteba nobw'ekeene, 33 Inwe mwatomete abanto ase Yohana, noborori bwaye nekeene. 34 Korende inche tindi konyora oborori korwa as'abanto: korende iga ngokwana aya erinde inwe mokonyeke. 35 Ere igarenge etaya egwoka nakomoreka: nainwe mwanchire koyosasokera omobaso oye ekero egeke. 36 Korende oborori nde naborobwo nobonene, kobua boria bwa Yohana: naki emeremo eria naetwe na Tata inyekore, emeremo eyio eyio nayekorire, yambereire kirori ng'a Tata nere ontomete. 37 Nere Tata ontomete obaire kirori asende. Eriogi riaye timwanya korigwa kero kende gionsi, gose ekieni kiaye timorakerora; 38 naende ring'ana riaye timori narirorio ime yaino: naki inwe timwancheti ere oyotomirwe nere. 39 Iga mokorigiarigia mono amariko, ekiagera mokagete ng'a inwe more nobogima bwa kare nakare ime yaye, nayio naro are kirori asende; 40 ko mwangire gocha asende, monyare koba nobogima. 41 Tindi konyora obonene as'abanto. 42 Korende nabsmanyire inwe ng'a timori nobwanchani bwa Nyasaye ime yaino. 43 Inche nachire as'erieta ria Tata one nainwe timori konyancha: oyonde karache as'eiieta riaye omonyene, namomwanche oyio. 44 Naki moranyare gwancha inwe abamokoenana obonene inwe as'inwe, nobonene boria bokorua ase Nyasaye ore bweka timori koborigia? 45 Timokaga ng'a inche nimbasoere ase Tata: nare oyokobasoera, nere Musa, oyomosemeretie inwe. 46 Naki onye mwamwanchete Musa, anga mwanyancha inche; ekiagera nere origete amang'ana ane. 47 Korende motayancheti amariko aye, naki morayanche amang'ana ane?

English: 1 After these things Jesus went over the Sea of Galilee, to Capernaum; 2 and a large crowd followed him, because they saw the signs he was performing on those who were sick. 3 Jesus got into a boat and crossed the sea to Capernaum. 4 Many people followed him, seeking his miracles. 5 When Jesus looked up and saw a great crowd coming toward him, he said to Philip, “Where shall we buy bread to feed them?” 6 He asked this only to test him, for he already knew what he was going to do. 7 Philip answered him, “Eight months’ wages would not buy enough bread for each of them to get a little.” 8 One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, spoke up. 9 “Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but what good are these for so many?” 10 Jesus said, “Tell them to sit down.” So he made the people sit down in the grass. There were about five thousand men there. 11 Then Jesus took the loaves and gave thanks, and distributed them to those who were seated, and likewise the fish as much as they wanted. 12 When everyone had eaten their fill, twelve baskets of broken pieces were collected. 13 They gathered them up, leaving none of the fish wasted. 14 When the people saw the sign he performed, they began saying, “Surely this is the Prophet who is coming into the world!” 15 But Jesus, knowing that they intended to come and make him king, withdrew again to the mountains by himself. 16 Later that evening, his disciples went down to the shore, and got into a boat and started across the lake toward Capernaum. It was already dark when a strong wind came up. 17 As they rowed, they struggled against the waves, because the wind was against them. 18 About three or four miles from land, they saw Jesus walking on the water and coming toward the boat. This terrified them. 19 But he said to them, “It is I; don’t be afraid.” 20 They were willing to take him aboard, and the boat reached the shore where they were heading. 21 The next day, the crowd that had stayed on the opposite side of the lake realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus hadn’t gone with them in it. 22 However, the following day, people who had remained on the other side of the lake gathered together and waited for Jesus, hoping he would come. 23 When they found him, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?” 24 Jesus replied, “Truly I tell you, you are looking for me not because you saw the signs I performed but because you ate the loaves and had your fill. 25 When they had crossed the lake, they came to Capernaum, and Jesus said to them, “Where did you get the bread?” 26 He answered, “Our father Jacob gave us this bread.” 27 Then Jesus told them, “I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty. 28 “But as I told you, you have seen me and still you do not believe. 29 All those the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never drive away. 30 So the Jews protested, “What sign can you show us to prove your authority?” 31 Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, Moses didn’t give your ancestors the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. 32 For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” 33 “Sir,” they said, “give us that bread continually.” 34 Jesus declared, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will not thirst. 35 “But as I have told you, you have seen me and yet you do not believe. 36 Very truly I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. 37 My Father gives them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand. 38 My Father has given them to me, and he has kept them safe. No one can take them from my Father’s hand. 39 My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all; no one can snatch them out of my Father’s hand. 40 And I have given them eternal life, and they will never perish; no one will snatch them out of my hand. 41 The Jews complained about him because he said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.” 42 They said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph? We know his father and mother. How can he say, ‘I came down from heaven’?” 43 Jesus replied, “Stop complaining among yourselves. 44 No one can come to me unless the Father draws them, and I will raise them up at the last day. 45 It is written in the Prophets: ‘They will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who listens to the Father and learns from him comes to me. 46 Not everyone has seen the Father; only the one who is sent by the Father has seen him. 47 “Very truly I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. 48 I am the bread of life. 49 Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness, yet they died. 50 But here is the bread that comes down from heaven, which anyone may eat and not die. 51 I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live forever. This bread is my flesh. 52 The Jews argued sharply among themselves, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” 53 Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. 54 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day. 55 For my flesh is real food and my blood is real drink. 56 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them. 57 As the living Father sent me and I live because of the Father, so whoever feeds on me will live because of me. 58 This is the bread that came down from heaven; your ancestors ate manna and died, but whoever eats this bread will live forever.” 59 He said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. 60 Many of his disciples turned back and no longer followed him. 61 Jesus said, “Does this offend you? Then what if you should see the Son of Man going back up where he came from? 62 What if you should see the Spirit ascending to where it came from? The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life. 63 But there are some among you who do not believe.” Jesus knew from the beginning which ones did not believe and who would betray him. 64 That is why he said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless the Father has enabled him.” 65 At this point many of his disciples turned away and stopped following him. 66 Jesus said, “Does this upset you? Then what about when you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was before? 67 The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life. 68 Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. 69 We have come to believe and to know that you are the Holy One of God.” 70 Jesus replied, “Have I not told you all this? Then why do you doubt my words? 71 It was Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, who betrayed him. One of his disciples was Judas, who betrayed him.
